newsitem.title: INDIA: India's SBI GDR clears hurdle - papers.
newsitem.headline: India's SBI GDR clears hurdle - papers.

text.p: The Indian finance ministry has approved a plan by the State Bank of India (SBI) to issue $500 million in global depository receipts (GDRs), newspapers said on Wednesday.
The proposal was expected to be taken up by the cabinet on Thursday, they said. Finance ministry officials could not be reached for comment.
The Financial Express said the ministry cleared the proposed GDR issue despite opposition from the Communist Party of India (Marxist), which is supporting Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's government.

The newspaper said critics of the proposed issue had said SBI's share price was too low to consider a GDR issue and that the bank was flush with funds due to increased deposit mobilisation and a larger return flow of capital from industry.
SBI shares closed at 261.25 rupees on the Bombay Stock Exchange last Friday.

The Economic Times said opponents of the GDR claimed the issue could permit foreign institutional investors eventually to hold up to a 34 percent stake in SBI, currently controlled by the Reserve Bank of India.
